contracts.title: Updater producer → supervisor readiness → full serve launch
body: Preflight binds the remote updater adapter to the main updater functions and publishes the app version before packaged PATH hydration. RPC exposes status/check/download/install; each handler delegates to the configured local runtime adapter. The shared WebSocket admission owns device authentication, and the mobile allowlist does not admit updater methods. An accepted install response is an admission snapshot, not a completed update.

Unpackaged/development, marked local preview, unsupported headless platforms, deb/rpm and unusable downloads have distinct unavailable/manual/deferred outcomes. Setup disables automatic downloads and restricts implicit quit installation to interactive non-root operation. Release feed and signing verification are external distribution roles; no original destination or credentials are transferred by this audit.

Installation deduplicates in-progress calls, clears pending timers, and performs deferral/refusal checks before irreversible cleanup. It sets state, awaits pre-quit cleanup, writes the supervisor handoff, then invokes native quit/install through launch-path handling. Failed handoff persistence resets state and refuses native invocation and PTY killing. Native invocation precedes in-process PTY cleanup; after native commitment, later failure keeps the handoff/watchdog rather than pretending rollback.

The canonical user-data handoff is a schema/version/PID-bound file written through a mode-0600 temporary file and rename. The environment path check is lexical resolve equality, not realpath identity; the producer itself is not an OS authorization guard. Write failures return false; no fsync, cross-process transaction or universal temporary-file cleanup is established. Failed handoff state applies only to the matching requesting PID/phase, and matching installed version clears its failure record.

The serve startup boundary awaits local PTY and provider readiness, registers headless PTYs, restores orchestration authority, reconciles legacy terminals, conditionally enables offscreen browser capability, publishes an empty headless window graph, then awaits RPC start. It installs repeated quit signal handling, attempts non-elevating CLI installation on Unix and a best-effort packaged Linux dispatcher, starts automation/history GC, and finally calls printServeReady. The latter requires runtime/RPC, validates recipe project when supplied, prepares pairing/advertised endpoint, awaits readiness publication, then sends orca:serve-ready over connected process IPC. A readiness message does not assert healthy managed WSL, every optional pairing path, rendered UI, or surviving daemon ownership. QR import failure remains outside its later QR-render catch.

Supervisor disconnect quits only under the serve/canonical-supervisor gate. send() has synchronous exception handling but no acknowledgement proof. Reuse accepted launch/supervisor replacement contracts and the newly read launch test tail; do not equate detached/unref, IPC-ready, native invocation, or a mock daemon.alive object with verified process survival.
contracts.boundary: WP-ENG-INSTALL owns updater native execution, supervisor replacement/watchdog and distribution verification; WP-ENG-CLI owns accepted launch.ts; WP-ENG-REMOTE owns actual execution-host/PTy restoration. Imported updater class scheduling, native autoUpdater and runtime internals are downstream, not re-audited.
tests: native replace timeout vs ready; early parent death; handoff mode/path/symlink/race and late write; commit before cleanup failure; reject manual-only/unsupported RPC install; failed printServeReady must not notify supervisor; optional WSL pending remains distinct; OS daemon/PTY survival and both launcher version skews

contracts.title: trustedOrcaHooks prompt, persistence and callers
body: ensureHooksConfirmed serializes modal work with a promise queue whose rejected predecessor does not poison the next prompt. Setup trust hashes trimmed setup plus indexed/labeled defaultTabs commands; VM recipe trust includes lifecycle declarations and identity/display fields. Repository-wide trust can bypass content inspection; duplicate repo IDs disable that wide bypass. Per-script trust remains keyed by repoId/script kind/content hash, with runtime or SSH owner selection supplied separately by the caller. Local-only and local issue-command paths bypass shared trust; shared inspection failure fails closed to skip.

Cancellation is checked before inspection/hash and before displaying a prompt; an already displayed modal has no general AbortSignal cancellation loop in this helper. The modal settles once, dismissal means skip, and always-trust state is reset on open. Run optionally records trust before resolving. UI trust actions clone/replace the map optimistically and fire window.api.ui.set with logging on rejection: they neither await durable save nor roll back the displayed trust state.

Desktop ui:set ignores the event identity at this handler and forwards typed partial updates to the profile store; this is not the stricter Skills IPC sender gate. Paired ui.set validates the strict outer schema but trustedOrcaHooks is only record<string,unknown>. It removes pairing-local fields; trustedOrcaHooks is not among those exclusions. Runtime updateUIState calls store update then immediately reads state. Persisted UI merges general durable updates, schedules saving and notifies; a trust map is replaced as a field, not transactionally merged across writers. E2 owns the accepted SP01–SP13 durable writer contract beyond this scheduling boundary.

Hydration rejects dangerous top-level keys/non-record values but does not validate every nested trust record. With no valid repo IDs yet, sanitized trust survives the pending catalog. Only a latest-generation successful all-host load prunes unknown repo IDs; local-first, remote failure and stale completion must preserve remote entries. Pruning updates renderer state and does not itself write the pruned map durably.

Full/quick composer preparation passes host/runtime identity and cancellation checks; skip can suppress setup and issue-command launch, and quick ask-policy can defer to the advanced UI. VM creation gates recipe launch on trust. Automation saves a skipped setup decision when trust is declined. Direct work-item launch calls ensureHooksConfirmed without the explicit host parameter used by composer, so duplicate-ID routing needs a discriminating test. Removal bypasses archive trust for forget-local and otherwise checks owner/generation after awaiting confirmation. These are caller-level contracts, not a claim that every subsequent creator, archive writer or provider operation is atomic.
contracts.boundary: E2 accepted settings/persistence/shortcut source gate; WP-ENG-WORKTREES and E1 own full composer/archive execution; WP-ENG-REMOTE owns host routing. Retain nested malformed map behavior, optimistic-save failures and concurrent whole-map updates as explicit acceptance obligations.
tests: same repo ID on two hosts with different content; repo-wide versus script trust isolation; UI save rejection then restart; concurrent edits do not silently erase trust; malicious nested values/prototype keys; all-host partial/failure/generation race; cancellation before/while modal; exact approved content versus target-branch changed hooks; paired-mobile trust write permissions

contracts.title: Setup environment and defaultTabs consumption
body: Setup environment provides four compatibility root/worktree path variables, workspace name, and the internal Git credential guard policy. Local runtime obtains effective created-worktree hooks, translates runHooks/setupDecision, and obtains defaultTabs separately. A default-tabs decision failure keeps templates with runCommands false; setup decision failures have different caller catches. Runner generation failure can return a successfully created worktree without launch, and the non-runner path can start a background hook through an imported runner with logged unsuccessful results.

Runner files live under git rev-parse --git-path per-worktree metadata. WSL paths map to UNC for Node filesystem writes. Script write is direct, not an atomic rename. Native Windows chooses cmd unless a usable POSIX shell and a shebang demand POSIX; interpreter choice and terminal launch shell are separate. Git Bash converts only the four path keys; the WSL loop applies Linux path conversion to all environment values, despite the narrower comment. POSIX mode is 0755 where supported. Wait behavior ORs local and project policy.

Runtime creates default tabs before setup, honors runCommands for trimmed template commands, and applies titles/colors. Each failed tab can leave preceding tabs; a color failure can leave an already collected handle. Setup uses split/new-tab policy, may create a primary fallback tab, and optionally observes completion with a UUID token/env. A returned PTY ID is needed to record observation. The outer catch allows partial state; there is no universal rollback.

Renderer application marks defaults applied before creating tabs, so failed creation does not automatically retry. First-tab startup command can override the first default command; remaining commands respect runCommands. Titles/colors, activation and queued setup/issue commands go through renderer-owned execution queues. This is distinct from main runtime provisioning and not proof both paths are deduplicated under reconnection.

Remote worktree setup reads the created tree's YAML through remote providers, creates the remote runner under remote Git metadata and chooses script format from the remote absolute path. Local-only shared/symlink/include behavior is explicitly separated in source. The local IPC path likewise reads created YAML and only writes the runner rather than invisibly executing it; runner failure after Git creation degrades to created-without-setup. Reuse accepted effective-hook parsing and policy helpers; preserve the mismatch possibility between trust inspected before creation and effective target-tree content.
contracts.boundary: WP-ENG-WORKTREES owns Git creation/provisioning and effective-hook decisions; WP-ENG-REMOTE owns fs/Git provider semantics; WP-ENG-TERMINAL/E1 own actual shell execution, command queues and completion. Imported script-text/parser/provider internals are explicit boundaries.
tests: run/skip/inherit/ask across CLI, desktop and SSH; defaultTabs no-command/title-only and denied commands; setup failure after committed Git create; partial tab/color failure and reconnect dedup; WSL value conversion versus Git Bash paths; Windows cmd/POSIX shebang/native shell; completion token with missing/late PTY; approved content drift

contracts.title: WSL guest installation, readiness transport and distro observation
body: Reuse accepted manager/launch/recovery/link/dependency wiring. Guest install records the attempt timestamp before awaiting hook installation and plugin request. Plugin overlay updates are fenced to the same mux: unavailable keeps prior knowledge, none clears, available replaces. Rerun requires current mux/home/not disposed and rate window. A nonempty returned plugin directory is accepted without whitespace canonicalization. Unknown-method, connection-lost/disposed and already-disposed mux are compatibility-unavailable outcomes, not proof the guest lacks plugins.

Hook detection preflight failure warns and returns. Codex follows its managed runtime-home path and is removed from the shared installer set; remaining detected agents use the remote managed installer. SFTP adaptation maps selected error codes and requires result.ok===true but is not itself filesystem schema or ownership enforcement. E4's provider-specific hook contracts supersede generic assumptions; native Windows SSH remains a distinct unsupported/unproved boundary.

Sentinel handshake buffers stdout until readiness, enforces the pre-sentinel byte budget, retains a bounded NUL-cleaned stderr tail, and rejects timeout/early close/error with a kill request. Bytes after a split sentinel are replayed in queued order, including before subscription. Post-ready pending chunks have no comparable queue limit in this adapter. Writes expose acceptance/callback/drain; late stdin errors are absorbed. close/kill request is not verified process exit, and no generic AbortSignal is supplied.

The WSL guest entry requires a positive integer hook port and a nonempty token; it starts a token-protected HTTP hook server through an imported helper, registers preflight/hook/fs methods, and publishes the primary stdio sentinel. It does not register the general PTY service. Stdin loss/stdout error/signals dispose and stop before exit; an uncaught exception exits, while an unhandled rejection is logged. The dispatcher identity defaults to unproved; HTTP token and stdio transport are different admission boundaries.

Reattach warming requires a proven local reattach with a nonempty distro from the result, never current preference or SSH connection. Running-distro cache collapses concurrent probes and backs off failures while retaining last known positive results or returning empty without prior cache; success, even empty, replaces cache. A synchronous probe throw is not covered by the promise catch. Non-Windows enumeration is empty without spawning. Neither cached membership nor an empty result on error proves live/exited.
contracts.boundary: WP-ENG-REMOTE owns distro/process authority and guest transport; E4 final hook source report owns exact provider writers; WP-ENG-RELAY owns request handlers; third-party WSL/ssh/SFTP APIs require real platform fixtures.
tests: real WSL stopped/running/missing distro and long outage without accidental wake; split sentinel/oversize/post-ready backpressure; timeout then late readiness/close; stale mux install completion and unavailable legacy guest; rate-limit failure retry; callback error/mode/ownership; Linux guest hook invocation; native Windows SSH separate; no cleanup on unverifiable host

contracts.title: Relay handler admission and cancellation retirement
body: Reuse the independent relay review's method lists, not the weaker leaf. Service wiring constructs shared PTY/fs/Git stream/watch contexts and registers preflight, skills, external automation, ports, agent execution and workspace session methods. AiVault initialization can throw; only explicit unsupported/absent cases are soft. Plugin identity absence degrades availability. Remote proxy routes exclude the origin and use per-method timeout. Session-root truthiness/casts and home expansion here are not auth/containment checks.

Dispatcher creates a client session identity, defaulting to unproved/unauthenticated. Request routing attaches identity, generation-stale predicate, AbortSignal and response-settlement callbacks to handlers; it does not universally enforce their permissions. Missing method is -32601; selected numeric errors survive, others become -32000; only specific structured error schemas are forwarded. rpc.cancel aborts the same client's request. Notification handlers have a different no-await path. A handler must enforce its own authenticated owner capabilities and validate parameters.

PTY open adapts several values coercively with Number/String and accepts optional objects without deep schema; requiring a session identity is not requiring authenticated=true. Reconnect transport delegates handshake verification, attaches credential/version-derived identity, backpressure and leftover data, and detaches on peer close. Loss of attachment is not a PTY exit verdict. Preserve Git 2.25 and both wire-version directions at downstream Git/fs/PTY handlers.

deliveryCanceled retirement is fenced by mux/token/client generation/owner generation/incarnation. Recovery-pending branches restore and wake. In the normal branch applySshPtySourceCancellationProof returns a boolean, including false if no installed intake, but the caller ignores it and then retires/deletes delivery state. Throws preserve a different outcome. This confirms the independent review's exact unanswered result-handling issue; it does not prove a live failure. The distinct recovery-proof branch must not be conflated with this one.

Owned-process disposal awaits skills then best-effort AiVault; handler disposal calls fs/Git cleanup with no universal catch. No broad claim that all registrations, subprocesses or watches have completed teardown is justified.
contracts.boundary: WP-ENG-RELAY owns dispatcher and concrete registered handlers; WP-ENG-REMOTE owns SSH identity/intake; Git/fs/PTY handlers and third-party adapters remain named implementation boundaries, not permission inherited from registration. E3 owns runtime schema/receiver linkage.

contracts.title: Mobile pairing journals and recovery authority
body: Strict journal metadata separates public offer/host/fingerprint/resume-hash fields from keychain device/invite/pending credentials. Creation generates random journal and pending token identities; schemas constrain shapes but do not prove token/hash correspondence. Stored offer cell/director strings are weaker than the canonical HTTPS endpoint schema used elsewhere.

Save/load are native-gated and serialize mutations within this module. Metadata is saved before secrets, so partial failure is possible. Missing/invalid metadata cleans secret best-effort; missing/mismatched secret clears metadata and secret with differing propagation. Replacement after a winner or authorization is refused; preauthorization replacement is allowed. Expected journal ID prevents stale mutation/clear. This is not a cross-process or transactional metadata/keychain store. Direct-upgrade journals have their own per-host keychain keys and credential-write revision tracking, with no shared serialization guarantee.

Recovery is single-flight, returns none on web, defers failed journal reads, and tries pending resume, distinct current resume, then unexpired invite. Authoritative committed status publishes recovered credentials; authoritative not-found on invite records the winner before provisioning using the same request/hash. It verifies the committed response after provisioning and closes each client. Director movement persists updated cell/epoch first. Observed commit followed by local write failure remains deferred; elapsed invite plus grace without observed commit may abandon, including when best-effort clear failed.

Local publication updates authorization metadata, writes credential bundle, saves host, then clears journal; earlier effects can survive a later failure. An existing same-host binding plus any found bundle can shortcut recovery; this module does not independently prove the bundle's identity equivalence. No user cancellation or universal deadline is owned here: transport/keychain/storage boundaries govern those operations.
contracts.boundary: WP-CAP-MOBILE owns native keychain/host storage and recovery; WP-ENG-REMOTE and WP-ENG-CLOUD own authoritative credential status/install, movement and E2EE. Dynamic wrapper names remain the independent review's 209 lower bound, not a new completeness total.
tests: crash at each metadata/keychain/bundle/host write; wrong-ID/hash/host bundle; stale clear and concurrent save; pending/current/invite recovery order; committed response lost; failed clear after expiry; moved endpoint origin/epoch verification; real native keychain and revoke/reconnect both version directions

contracts.title: Mobile request → authenticated host → desktop relay service
body: RpcClient retains string method/unknown params for requests and subscriptions; the relay session forwards those names after a connection budget, while stream subscription uses a separate stream owner. Resume hello must match expected kind/version; only authenticated link callbacks advance toward confirmation. The remainder of E2EE link/stream/request-budget execution is a named transport boundary, not closed by these first 135 lines.

Host WebSocket routing parses JSON, checks request identity/method and bound versus request token, validates device registry credentials, then applies the explicit mobile scope allowlist. A parsed JSON null is not structurally guarded before property access. Admission of a method name is not its payload validation. Long-poll leases and WebSocket abort registration wrap streaming dispatch and are disposed in finally. Pairing authorization context is supplied only from an authenticated socket through the configured context provider.

Pairing getEndpoints/provision use strict shared schemas and refuse missing authorization context. Endpoint schema requires canonical HTTPS origins, safe epoch, version/framing and bounded identity shapes; nested request-ID equality is not universally refined. Desktop relay service requires E2EE keys and mobile wiring, holds demand/revoke ledger state, and constructs an auth coordinator and broker with profile user/profile/org identity and refresh callbacks.

Authenticated direct connections may authorize direct installation. Relay invite connections on this host provide basis authority; resume-relay does not gain provisioning authority. Local-only or non-mobile provision refuses, as do missing broker/endpoints, wrong host and absent install basis. Binding persistence precedes broker installation and is not rolled back here. Resume confirmation is restricted to resume-relay endpoints.

Revocations flush only for the matching host/owner, removing outbox records after acknowledgement; failed flush retains retry evidence. Transient broker demand releases in finally; stop clears timers and coordinator state. Fence clears liveness and fences coordinator, but demand-expiry handling is a separate timer path. These modules expose owned lifecycle but do not establish backend auth-coordinator, credential DB or physical E2EE correctness.
contracts.boundary: E3 owns final schema/receiver joins; WP-CAP-MOBILE owns request/stream transport and actual call sites; WP-ENG-REMOTE owns desktop relay coordinator/broker; WP-ENG-CLOUD owns durable credential authorization. Unbounded/computed client calls remain source-unknown, not deleted.

contracts.title: Cloud relay factory, boot configuration and shutdown
body: Leaf full app/auth-verifier body evidence is adopted only with the corrections below. Relay role is combined/director/cell, not just director/cell. Public assign/resolve/regions reject cell role, while many admin mutations specifically require director; host drain specifically requires cell. /assign verifies an ES256 host-control JWT and matching body host identity, then uses sticky or placement admission, signs a five-minute HS256 cell assignment lease and releases admission in finally. /resolve instead validates a resume credential through the credential store and uses the reserved admission lane; it does not use the host JWT verifier.

Admin middleware rejects a verified identity on a disallowed route; missing/unverified bearer continues to route-specific authentication. Dedicated deploy/capacity/Asia-proof/monitor/fence/fence-broker route roles are distinct from heartbeat runtime and regional-rehome audience/identity checks. Read-only evacuation-status callers cannot request completeReady mutation. Missing audiences fail closed in relevant verifiers. Unknown thrown errors are not all conflicts: handling is route-specific; public typed capacity/database errors return 503 and other failures rethrow.

Config requires signing key material, issuer/JWKS/audience roles, distinct configured admin identities, paired rehome identity/audience, distinct rehome/runtime identity, unique nonempty director cells, canonical HTTPS origins except loopback HTTP, and paired connection cap/unobserved-bound with remaining admission. Non-cell admission concurrency must leave database headroom and both lanes must fit. Runtime identity can fall back to deploy; heartbeat audience can derive from director/public origin. Do not reproduce literal destinations or reuse the source's credentials.

Executable index loads config, opens database, reconciles startup admission, then constructs server/session/credential/assignment services. It starts unref'd credential cleanup and role-owned assignment/inventory sweeps, observability, regional rehome and heartbeat before listen. SIGTERM/SIGINT clear timers, stop these helpers, drain sessions at zero and close server before database close callback. Startup throws/listen error and database close rejection are not normalized into a universal graceful result here; no global forced shutdown deadline is installed.

Durable assignment, credential, server WebSocket handshake, database and migration operations are explicit injected/imported owners. Region cache/admission/rejection log are local factory state, not persisted authority. The Dockerfile builds contract before relay with frozen lockfile and runs as node; an image tag/base reference does not establish artifact provenance or a completed build.
contracts.boundary: WP-ENG-CLOUD: relay-server.ts, assignment-store.ts, store/database, admission/heartbeat/rehome implementations. Their transactional fencing and live IAM enforcement remain downstream source/integration obligations; source shape alone cannot prove a requested Terraform state or plan belongs to the caller.
tests: JWT issuer/audience/algorithm/email-role matrix over actual server; combined/director/cell route matrix; invalid content-length versus oversized actual body; sticky outage cannot consume placement lane; release after throw; config invalid identity/cap/pool/origin; start failure resource cleanup; SIGTERM during in-flight migration and real DB close

contracts.title: Fence broker request, durable lease and privileged child command
body: Broker entry loads validated config before serving. It owns health and two mutation routes, with no in-app bearer authentication. Terraform declares restricted invoker roles; that is intended deployment policy, not proof nobody else can reach a live instance. Strict confirmation/image commit/target/recovery shape checks precede lease acquire, operation and release. Conflict maps to 409; generic failures map to 500 and an operation failure leaves the lease held. Release failure can report 500 after operation success. Self-target rejection is an explicit route guard, separate from the schema's duplicate-target refine.

Config requires bounded port/project/lease paths/service-account roles and a 40-hex image commit; director must be canonical origin and admin audience the same origin's drain path. This check does not itself insist on HTTPS. Source, failed and replacement cells must differ. The broker image includes pinned Terraform version, cloud SDK base, built Node code, deployment scripts and Terraform tree, then runs as an unprivileged broker user; provider IAM still authorizes its external effects.

GCS lease hashes JSON.stringify(request), validates existing record/generation and writes with ifGenerationMatch. New lease uses generation zero, expiry is 35 minutes; exact expected generation/operation/digest authorizes live takeover, expired leases can be replaced, and an identical request digest can replace an unexpired lease. A 412 is conflict. Metadata and object media are read separately without a generation-pinned media read; CAS guards publication but not an assumed atomic read snapshot. Release is generation-conditional, tolerates 404 and otherwise propagates failure. No renewal, abort signal or hard operation timeout is supplied.

Runner makes a temporary directory, invokes terraform init with input disabled and production backend, reads deployment topology to a mode-0600 file, obtains metadata identity token and service-account email, then executes node deploy-relay-gce-multi-target.mjs with fixed production mode/var-file, source/targets, commit and minimum lease remaining. Target lists sort; recovery adds all attempt/state/generation/hash pins. Temporary directory removal is in finally, whose failure can mask prior errors. execFile limits output to 10 MiB but has no explicit timeout/cancellation. Metadata requests validate response shapes but have no explicit timeout.

Helper supports separate read/mutation token parameters, but the actual runner supplies the same broker token to both. Credential roles are metadata access for GCS, broker ID token for relay read/mutation, configured requester identity and runtime identity; no values are copied. The deployment script owns actual GCE/Terraform mutation and rollback, not the argument builder.
contracts.boundary: WP-ENG-CLOUD owns dev/scripts/deploy-relay-gce-multi-target.mjs and its fence-plan/operation verification imports, provider API and Terraform state. Same-request lease retry, concurrent revisions, operation beyond TTL and failed release require explicit integration proof.
tests: both routes MutationLeaseConflict→409; generic acquire/release failure precedence; identical-request concurrent lease replacement; expired versus exact live takeover; metadata/media generation race; operation beyond TTL; cancellation while child runs; real immutable plan/state/operation pins; failure after successful mutation must not trigger blind retry

contracts.title: Complete relay-contract export boundary
body: The index exports 14 modules, correcting the leaf's 12 claim. Leaf read director messages, admission budgets, regions and limits; lead read every remaining export body. This completes this finite package's source contract boundary, not all consumers. Scalars constrain canonical HTTPS, byte-encoded token/key shapes, bounded IDs and safe epochs. Strict host hello/challenge/ack, connection ticket, invite, refresh/drain and credential install/status/resume schemas retain exact optional/absent and invite-versus-resume variants.

Control loss prefers matching-secret rebind even with a competing generation, otherwise fences old or enters orphan grace. New work requires active and unexpired auth; refresh must preserve user/profile/org/host identity. Pure invite transitions preserve rollback identity, invalidate on direct install, consume on provision, enforce reservation attempts/cooldown/expiry and strip lease fields. They do not execute the declared DB transaction. Resume decisions distinguish current renewal, unchanged grace, retired, expired and revoked.

Assignment activity sums all six work classes before normal dormant reassignment; evacuation requires different cells, reserved target capacity and epoch+1. Splice forward transitions prohibit skips and require forwarding handlers before acknowledging a host-attached client. Confirmation tuple preserves owning generation/device/version/deadline. Host proof serializes length-tagged fields with domain separation and validates byte lengths; serialization is not cryptographic verification, and safe numeric/origin admission belongs to the caller.

Constants for timing/capacity/frame bounds and declared atomic effects remain source compatibility obligations. No source-level schema, helper test or declaration proves real transaction rollback, token secret correspondence, host possession or every consumer's enforcement.
contracts.boundary: WP-ENG-CLOUD owns service consumers/database transactions; WP-ENG-REMOTE/WP-CAP-MOBILE own cryptographic handshake and moved-origin consumption. Caller completeness for isTrustedNewerMove remains a named source join, not the leaf's guessed SSH location.
tests: port unchanged contract and persistence-invariant suites; malformed/extra/absent/null fields; host-proof byte/domain collision and unsafe scalar caller admission; real transaction idempotency/deadlocks; invite direct/relay race; migration epoch and resume-current/grace matrix in both mixed-version directions

contracts.title: Infra selection, operations UI and named workflow boundaries
body: Leaf relay.tf/fence-broker.tf declarations establish runtime/director identities, signing-key and placement-flag secret roles, service env cross-wiring and pool preconditions. Lead resolves production-ops gate: configured GitHub owner/repo and environment production. Workload trust builds repository/name/ID/owner-ID conjunctions with per-repository workflow arms; actual ref/environment/event restrictions and provider IAM bodies remain their named files, not inferred from this renderer.

Cell selection is not source-unknown in the way the leaf stated: nonempty GCE domain plus cells selects GCE topology for director cells; otherwise Cloud Run cell definitions are selected. Fenced GCE cell target size becomes zero, others one. This is a source selection rule, not proof which deployed environment is authoritative or that both compute paths run simultaneously. GCE network uses private subnets/NAT; remaining template/firewall/startup/DNS/database/observability/IAM plan effects are explicit infra-owner boundaries.

Ops index binds loopback with no user login layer, serves security/no-store headers and bounded snapshot query parameters; snapshot errors become 503. Staging controls require an explicit environment flag, exact loopback Origin and timing-safe CSRF token before strict mode/confirmation parsing. Accepted means gh workflow dispatch succeeded, not infrastructure completion. The helper has 30s timeout/output cap and redacts its process failure into a generic error. Dashboard/cache/gcloud clients are delegated data boundaries.

Ops environment data eagerly reads the repository Terraform tfvars and parses cell blocks with regex plus selected enums, rather than evaluating HCL; missing required fields throw. Imported repository/prefix constants determine the target workflow repository. That imported-tree deployment convention is distinct from the current .github cloud-prefixed source path and needs a packaged/repository-move fixture.

Broker deploy workflow is manual/main/operations-enabled/production, non-cancelling shared rollout concurrency, with OIDC deploy identity and rollout lease action. It verifies supplied digest and exact source-SHA tag before image-only service update, then checks ready singleton traffic and served image. There is no rollback block in this workflow. Power workflow is scheduled sleep or manual mode under staging non-cancelling mutation concurrency; OIDC/rollout lease precede topology init/output, exact manual mutation confirmation precedes power script. Script owns activity-zero refusal and actual power effects.

Recovery requeue workflow has actions-write authority, responds only to cancelled main recovery runs, requires exactly one cancelled recover job that never started, and avoids dispatch if another run has passed gate with recover active; otherwise dispatches the fixed recovery confirmation. It only examines the returned 100-run page, so no universal concurrency proof is claimed. Remaining cloud workflow bodies and ops CLI entrypoints are source-unknown downstream entries, retained explicitly rather than counted closed by these three workflows.
